title: Common Camellia: Ancient Camellias You Can Visit
meta_description: A shrub in a pot almost everywhere. Japan's thickest wild camellia, in a village burial ground in Himi, is 3.89 metres round.
intro: A camellia is supposed to drop its flower whole, head and all, which is why samurai were said to dislike them. The four hundred year old tree at Byakugo-ji in Nara does not: it sheds petal by petal, and it opens red, white, peach, striped and variegated blossoms on the same plant. Japan's thickest wild camellia stands in a village burial ground at the end of a dead-end valley in Himi, three trunks grown back into each other and 3.89 metres round; its age is put at 500 years by the city and 700 to 800 by an older survey. Portugal is the other home of old camellias. The mild wet north suited Camellia japonica so well that Portuguese growers ended up exporting it back to the rest of Europe, and the pair in front of the church at Paranhos in Porto are six and a half metres tall.
